newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close strong, pork bellies sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close strong, pork bellies sharply higher.

text.p: CME hog futures finished strong and pork belly futures sharply higher as reduced kills from tight hog numbers prompted ideas of a stronger pork product market, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.825 to 0.025 cent higher paced by April with December up 0.575 at 59.500 and February up 0.550 at 77.525 cents. Pork bellies ended 2.425 to 1.350 cents higher with February up 2.025 at 79.300 cents.
Expectations of continued tight hog numbers and an oversold condition Friday boosted hog futures. Light runs will keep slaughter down and support pork products, traders said.

Packers are expected to bid up for hogs Tuesday after paying better than expected prices on Monday. Most interior markets were steady to instances weak Monday after early calls for lower live prices, they said.

Expectations for hog marketings to remain tight into next year also lent support, especially to nearby lean contracts. Traders said there appears to be some early positioning before the upcoming Hog and Pig report at the end of the month.
"The outlook is that we will still have fewer hogs for the next three, four, or five month," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Levitt is also looking for hog futures to gain on live cattle futures and there may be some spreading in this vein.

In hog options, locals bought calls and sold puts on the rally. Volatility was firm in February through June. E.D.&F. Man and ADM Investor Services bought June 68 and 70 puts late. Smith Barney did the February 73/78 straddle, selling 73 calls and 78 puts, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures also benefited from ideas of continued reduced hog runs and slaughter which would strengthen cash belly prices. Cash product was a little easier at noon, but expected to firm by Tuesday, traders said.
"I'm hearing that it's (cash belly market) firming and it's going to be higher by this evening and certainly higher by tomorrow morning," Levitt said.

The light hog kill ideas also encouraged talk that product would not be moving into storage at the usual pace for this time of year. Demand from fast food outlets is also remains quite high, traders added.
Rand Financials and Cargill Investor Services were notable buyers during the day, pit sources added.
